name: Amzi
overview: Amzi was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically descending from the Merarite clan through Mushi, son of Merari. He is uniquely identified as the son of Bani, situating him within the Levitical genealogies that emphasize priestly and temple service roles. This lineage highlights his connection to the sacred duties assigned to the Levites in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Amzi is a proper name meaning '[poss.] [y-h-v-h is] my strength,' reflecting a common theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord as the source of strength. This meaning underscores the believer's reliance on God’s power, although the name itself was not explicitly given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Amzi as the son of Bani and infers Hilkiah as his father, establishing a clear paternal lineage within the Levitical family. Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amzi’s significance lies in his role as a descendant of the Merarite branch of the Levites, a tribe set apart for specific service in the tabernacle and later the temple. His genealogy, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:46, contributes to the biblical record that preserves the heritage and responsibilities of those who ministered to God’s people. This lineage supports the continuity of priestly service essential to Israel’s worship and covenantal life.
